datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @default(now())
  body      String
  article   Article  @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

content.text:
**Review of the comment edit change (`updateComment`, `PUT /articles/:slug/comments/:id`)**

I found no written rule for any of the four questions. The repo's only prose is `app/README.md`, which links to the external RealWorld spec and to a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` that is not in the working directory. So I could not PASS or FLAG the rules themselves. Where the code shows a convention, I say so, but a convention is not a rule.

**1. Edit time window.** UNVERIFIED. No rule in the repo sets how long after creation a comment can be edited. `updateComment` (`app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts:527`) has no time check. Assumption: no window applies. If the team has one, the diff breaks it, because any comment can be edited at any time.

**2. Edited mark and migration.** UNVERIFIED. No rule in the repo says how an edited comment is marked. `schema.prisma` has no edited flag. `Comment.updatedAt` is `@default(now())` without `@updatedAt`, so the service sets it by hand at line 564. The diff adds no migration, and the four existing migrations add no mark. If the team requires a dedicated flag, the diff does not provide one.

**3. API error shape and status codes.** UNVERIFIED as a rule. `app/src/main.ts:42` sends `err.message` as the body with the error's status. The code uses several shapes:
- `{ errors: { field: [...] } }` for 422 (`auth.service.ts:45`, `article.service.ts:175`, and the diff at line 529).
- `{ errors: { article: ['not found'] } }` for 404 (`article.service.ts:270`).
- `{}` for 404 (`article.service.ts:307`, and the diff at line 549).
- `{ message: '...' }` for 403 (`article.service.ts:615`, and the diff at line 553).
- `{ errors: {...} }` for 403 (`auth.service.ts:124`).

The status codes in the diff (422, 404, 403) are all already in use. The 403 body is the one that differs from the `errors` convention. I did not flag it because no rule decides it.

**4. Ownership, and what is returned for not found or another user's comment.**
- Owner: the comment's author, `Comment.authorId` in `schema.prisma`. This matches the diff's check at line 553.
- Not found: the diff returns 404 (line 549). This matches `deleteComment` (line 611) and `profile.service.ts:16`.
- Belongs to someone else: the diff returns 403 (line 553). `deleteComment` returns 404 in this case, because its query filters on author id. The code disagrees with itself here, and no written rule settles it. The rule owner needs to choose between 403 and 404.

**Verdict: NOT APPROVED.** Rules 1 and 2 could not be checked, and the change does not implement a mark or a window. Rule 4 has two code precedents that disagree.
